clue.text: Arab in charge in troubled times offers truce

parts.note: Ar is a standard abbreviation for Arab or Arabic

indicators.note: the second 'in' places one piece inside the other, the way a thing sits in a box
something troubled is disturbed and thrown into disorder, so the letters that follow are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be mixed up
i/c is the usual shorthand for in charge

explanation.surface: An Arab leader, in a period of unrest, proposes a ceasefire.
explanation.walkthrough: AR comes first, then the jumbled TIMES (MISTE) has IC slipped in near its end: AR + MIST(IC)E.
explanation.definitionFit: An armistice is a formal agreement between warring sides to stop fighting, which is exactly a truce.

clue.text: Venue for races in Nova Scotia?

indicators.note: 'in' says the answer sits inside the run of letters that follows, spanning the word break

parts.note: the letters run across the end of Nova and the start of Scotia

explanation.surface: A question about where a horse race might be held in the Canadian province.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that Nova Scotia is not a real location here, just a carrier. Ascot is a famous racecourse in Berkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Ascot Racecourse hosts Royal Ascot, one of Britain's best-known horse-racing meetings, so it is a place where races are run.

clue.text: Toast partner in awfully lame drama

indicators.note: doing something awfully means doing it badly, so the following letters are messed up

parts.note: the nine letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic raising a glass to a co-star in a terrible play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toast' looks like a drinking salute to a partner, but it is breakfast toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Marmalade is the classic spread eaten on toast at breakfast, its natural companion.

clue.text: Second outing with extremely outgoing male creature delivering sexy message?

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for second
a trip is an excursion or outing

indicators.note: 'extremely' points to the outermost letters of the next word, its two ends only

parts.note: first and last letters of outgoing
a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A cheeky ram on a jaunt bringing a saucy greeting.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the definition is loose: a stripogram is a novelty greeting delivered by someone who strips.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripogram is a birthday or party greeting performed by a stripper, so it is a risqué kind of message.

clue.text: Setter's not as ruddy as Vlad!

definitions.note: a proper name standing for the epithet the impaler

parts.note: the setter speaks of themself: I'm, the setter is
less ruddy in complexion means paler

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to being whiter-faced than Vlad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter's' is 'the setter is', so I'M. Vlad III of Wallachia, the model for Dracula, was known as Vlad the Impaler.
explanation.definitionFit: The Impaler was the historical nickname of Vlad III, a Wallachian prince notorious for executing enemies on stakes.

clue.text: Country ain't so bothered after introduction of euro

indicators.note: an introduction is the opening, so only the first letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the opening letter of euro

indicators.note: being bothered means being upset or ruffled, so the words before are jumbled

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A nation unbothered by adopting the single currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' places the jumbled letters after the E. Estonia did in fact adopt the euro in 2011, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Estonia is a Baltic state in northern Europe, a sovereign nation.

clue.text: Drug in pack of dairy product

indicators.note: 'in' tells us one item is placed inside the other, as goods go in a pack

parts.note: to cram is to pack tightly
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Narcotics smuggled inside a carton of milk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack' is a verb here, CRAM, not the carton the surface suggests; E goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Cream is the fat-rich layer skimmed from milk, a standard product of the dairy.

clue.text: Credit two points to gang

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
two compass points, east and west

explanation.surface: Awarding a couple of points to a team of youths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Points' in crosswords are often compass points: here E and W.
explanation.definitionFit: A crew is a group of people working or hanging out together, much like a gang.

clue.text: Caramel item contains 6 across

definitions.note: a cross-reference to CREAM in its sense of the best

indicators.note: the phrase before holds the answer inside itself, spread over the join of its two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of caramel and the start of item

explanation.surface: A toffee sweet is made with cream, as a recipe note.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 across is CREAM, but the link is the sense 'the cream of the crop', the best people, not the dairy sense the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: The cream of a group is its finest members, the same idea as the elite, the select top tier.

clue.text: I defy Mr to join Women's Institute for training to work in obstetrics

indicators.note: training shapes and reforms something, so the letters gathered are reorganised

parts.note: taken as written
WI is the usual abbreviation for the Women's Institute

explanation.surface: A woman defies her husband by signing up with a women's club to study childbirth.
explanation.walkthrough: The Women's Institute is a British community organisation for women. 'Training' looks like the course of study, but it signals the shuffle; the final 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Midwifery is the profession of assisting women in childbirth, the practical work of obstetric care.

clue.text: End of life's not part of job for nurse

indicators.note: saying something is not part of a whole means it is removed from it

parts.note: a career is one's profession or job

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, so only that one is taken

parts.note: final letter of life

explanation.surface: A sombre remark that death is no concern of a nurse's work.
explanation.walkthrough: Take an E out of CAREER to leave the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A carer looks after someone sick or disabled, so as a verb-turned-noun sense it matches a nurse.

clue.text: Rotten place for arbitrator to die horribly

parts.note: to put is to place

indicators.note: something done horribly is done badly, so the word before is scrambled

parts.note: a ref (referee) arbitrates in sport
the letters to be mixed up

explanation.surface: A grim football ground where the referee meets a nasty end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Place' reads as a noun in the surface but is the verb PUT.
explanation.definitionFit: Putrefied means decayed and decomposing, so it describes something that has gone rotten.

clue.text: Around noon, damaged arm, toe and lip bouncing on this?

definitions.note: a cryptic pointer to the thing one bounces on

indicators.note: 'around' means wrapped about something, so the next item goes inside
damaged things are knocked out of shape, so the body parts listed are rearranged

parts.note: the three body parts to be mixed up; 'and' just lists them
N is the abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A midday accident leaves someone with a hurt arm, toe and lip from bouncing.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue doubles as the definition: injuries from bouncing hint at where the bouncing happened.
explanation.definitionFit: A trampoline is a sprung canvas sheet on a frame, used for bouncing and somersaulting.

clue.text: Sound of city in shop?

indicators.note: the sound of a word is how it is spoken, so the answer is said like the city

parts.note: Delhi is the Indian capital city

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about urban noise heard inside a store.
explanation.definitionFit: A deli, short for delicatessen, is a shop selling cooked meats, cheeses and prepared foods.

clue.text: Mass includes poem translated by old boy in special vehicle

indicators.note: to include is to take inside, so the items that follow go within the first

parts.note: a pile is a mass or heap

indicators.note: translating changes a text's form, so the word before is put into a new order

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: A church service features a translated verse read by a former pupil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' is tempting as the church service, which suits the answer, but it is just a heap that holds the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The popemobile is the specially built vehicle, often with a bulletproof glass cabin, used to carry the Pope in public.

clue.text: Stupid mistake of cardinal disembowelled for deadly sin

indicators.note: disembowelling removes the insides, leaving only the outer shell of the word

parts.note: first and last letters of cardinal
anger (wrath) is one of the seven deadly sins

explanation.surface: A gory tale of a church cardinal executed for his sinfulness.
explanation.walkthrough: A clanger is British slang for an embarrassing blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop a clanger is a British idiom for making a conspicuous, foolish error.

clue.text: Girl taking bigwig to site of disaster

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within, so the second item goes inside the first

parts.note: Cheryl is a girl's name
a nob is a person of high status, a bigwig

explanation.surface: A young woman escorting an important person somewhere grim.
explanation.walkthrough: Nob is British slang for a toff or someone of high rank.
explanation.definitionFit: Chernobyl in Ukraine was the location of the 1986 nuclear reactor explosion, the worst nuclear accident in history.

clue.text: Supporter of new system to keep office in beer

indicators.note: 'in' places the first item inside the second, like a thing kept in a glass

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
a post is an office or position

explanation.surface: A reformer who wants the bar to stock beer in the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: An apostle is a vigorous advocate of a new idea or policy, extended from the early followers spreading Christianity.

clue.text: Way of dealing with mate in trouble in river

indicators.note: the second 'in' puts the scrambled piece inside the river

parts.note: the Trent is a major river in the English Midlands

indicators.note: being in trouble suggests disorder, so the word before is mixed up

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: How to handle a friend who has got into difficulties out on the water.
explanation.walkthrough: The River Trent flows through the English Midlands to the Humber.
explanation.definitionFit: Treatment is the manner in which someone or something is handled or dealt with.

clue.text: Raise for scoffed-at eastern currency

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
the lev is the currency of Bulgaria
to scoff food is to eat it greedily

explanation.surface: Seeking a pay rise for a currency that has been ridiculed in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoffed-at' reads as mocked, but split it: scoffed means ate, and 'at' puts it after the eastern currency.
explanation.definitionFit: To elevate something is to lift it higher, a direct synonym of raise as a verb.

clue.text: Got pier redeveloped as means to boost one's image

indicators.note: redeveloping a site rebuilds it in a new layout, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaside resort renovates its pier to improve its reputation.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an activity undertaken mainly to flatter oneself and enhance one's self-importance.

clue.text: Theatrical setting for central characters in Moscow government leaving power

indicators.note: the central characters of a word are its middle letters only

parts.note: the middle two letters of Moscow

indicators.note: something leaving departs, so that letter is dropped from the next word

parts.note: energy is power
G is an abbreviation for government

explanation.surface: A stage design built around key figures in a Russian regime losing their grip.
explanation.walkthrough: G is a standard abbreviation for government; it drops out of the word for power.
explanation.definitionFit: Scenery is the painted backdrops and structures on a stage that represent where the action takes place.

clue.text: Ignoramus ultimately gaining first in philosophy gets stick for untidy mark on page

indicators.note: 'ultimately' means in the end, so only the last letter is used

parts.note: the last letter of ignoramus

indicators.note: the first in a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the opening letter of philosophy
to lodge is to become stuck or fixed in place

explanation.surface: A dunce who finally gets a philosophy degree is mocked for blotting the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A splodge is a large irregular blot or smear, such as an ink stain left on paper.

clue.text: Relative swallows a piece of bread

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the next item goes within the first

parts.note: nan is an informal word for grandmother
taken as written

explanation.surface: A family member gulps down a mouthful of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: The bread being swallowed in the surface is in fact the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Naan is a flat, leavened Indian bread baked in a tandoor oven, served in individual pieces.

clue.text: Prize from a raffle rejected

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word before is read backwards

parts.note: a draw is a raffle or lottery

explanation.surface: A winner turns down the prize they won in a raffle.
explanation.definitionFit: An award is something given in recognition of merit, a synonym of prize.

clue.text: Court beginning to liquidate throws out defunct retailer

parts.note: to court someone is to woo them

indicators.note: 'out' suggests something put out of order, so the preceding word is rearranged
the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of liquidate
the letters to be mixed up

explanation.surface: A judge ordering a firm's liquidation discards its assets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' reads as a law court, but it is the verb WOO. Woolworths was a British high-street chain that went into administration and closed in 2009.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolworths was a well-known UK chain store selling general goods, which collapsed in 2008-09.

clue.text: Healthy food for boy found by Salvation Army?

parts.note: SA is the abbreviation for the Salvation Army
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A charity provides wholesome meals for a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found by' just means placed beside, here with the boy coming second.
explanation.definitionFit: A salad of raw vegetables or leaves is a typical example of nutritious, healthy eating.

clue.text: Unoccupied part of horrid Leeds

indicators.note: 'part of' says the answer is a section of the letters that follow, spanning two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of horrid and the start of Leeds

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark about an empty bit of an unloved northern city.
explanation.walkthrough: Leeds is a city in Yorkshire, northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle means not busy or not in use, so an idle person or machine is unoccupied.

clue.text: Drunk has something to climb into resting place

indicators.note: putting one thing into another places it inside, so the first item goes within the second

parts.note: a bed is a place for resting
a ladder is something you climb

explanation.surface: A tipsy person clambers up into bed.
explanation.walkthrough: Bladdered is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Bladdered is informal British slang meaning heavily intoxicated, so it is a synonym of drunk.

clue.text: One portion's just right

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a deal is a share or portion, as in a great deal

explanation.surface: Someone declares a single serving to be the perfect amount.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideal means perfect or most suitable, exactly as good as needed.

clue.text: Projection of Flintoff's second boundary

indicators.note: 'second' picks out one letter only, the one in position two of the word

parts.note: the second letter of Flintoff
an edge is a border or boundary

explanation.surface: A cricket pundit predicts Andrew Flintoff's next boundary hit.
explanation.walkthrough: Andrew Flintoff is a former England cricketer; a boundary in cricket is a shot reaching the edge of the field, but here it simply means edge.
explanation.definitionFit: A ledge is a narrow shelf that juts out from a wall or cliff, a projection.

clue.text: Made impossible prince stable lad

parts.note: Pr is an abbreviation for prince
even means steady or stable
Ted is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A royal and a stable lad were stopped, as in a horse-racing yard scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stable lad' looks like one phrase, a groom in a racing yard, but it splits into two separate pieces of wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To prevent something is to stop it from happening, rendering it impossible.
